result: DSCAM and DSCAML1 interact with PDZ domain-containing proteins via their C-termini, and deletion of the C-terminal 10 amino acids disrupts this interaction while maintaining proper protein localization.
evaluation: Claims C1, C2, C60, and C61 collectively demonstrate that DSCAM/DSCAML1 have PDZ-interacting motifs (C1), deletion disrupts PDZ binding (C2), MAGI proteins interact with DSCAM (C60), and the mutant proteins still localize to the cell surface (C61). The co-immunoprecipitation data (Figure 1B) and yeast two-hybrid results provide strong experimental support.

result: Dscam∆C/∆C mice are viable with stable DSCAM protein expression and show an intermediate retinal phenotype between wild-type and null mutants.
evaluation: Claims C3-C6 demonstrate that Dscam∆C/∆C mice survive (C3), express normal levels of DSCAM protein (C4), show proper protein localization (C5), and have modest retinal expansion (C6). Western blot (Figure 1C), immunofluorescence (Figure 1D-F), and histology (Figure 1H) provide converging evidence for this intermediate phenotype.

result: Dopaminergic (DA) amacrine cells in Dscam∆C/∆C mice show complete loss-of-function phenotypes indistinguishable from Dscam-/- mutants in cell density, spacing, and neurite fasciculation.
evaluation: Claims C7, C8, C27, and C28 demonstrate that DA cells have increased density and disrupted spacing (C7), are indistinguishable from null mutants by all measures (C8), show severe fasciculation in ∆C mutants but not in Bax-/- (C27, C28). Quantitative analyses (Figures 2D-G, 6M) and Elo scoring provide robust statistical support.

result: bNOS-positive amacrine cells in Dscam∆C/∆C mice develop nearly normally with minimal disruption in cell spacing, density, fasciculation, or stratification.
evaluation: Claims C9, C10, C32, and C33 show that bNOS cells have little disruption in organization (C9), maintain normal spacing and density (C10), show minimal fasciculation (C32), and stratify normally (C33). Multiple quantitative measures (Figure 2K-N) and imaging data (Figures 6, 7A-B) consistently support near-normal development.

result: Intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells (ipRGCs) in Dscam∆C/∆C mice show intermediate phenotypes with cell body clustering more severe than Bax-/- mutants but less severe than Dscam-/- mutants, and layer-specific differences in dendrite fasciculation.
evaluation: Claims C11-C13, C24, C29-C30 demonstrate that ipRGCs are severely affected in null mutants (C11), show intermediate clustering in ∆C mutants (C12), have non-significant density increases (C13), are more clustered than Bax-/- (C24), and show layer-specific fasciculation differences (C29-C30). DRP, Voronoi, and Elo analyses (Figures 3, 5, 6) provide quantitative support for this intermediate phenotype.

result: Cdh3-GFP retinal ganglion cells in Dscam∆C/∆C mice develop normally without increased cell density, clustering, or dendrite fasciculation.
evaluation: Claims C14, C15, and C31 show that Cdh3-GFP RGCs have normal cell numbers (C14), no clustering (C15), and no fasciculation (C31) in ∆C mutants. Multiple spacing measures (Figure 3K-N) and Elo scoring (Figure 6—figure supplement 1) consistently demonstrate normal development.

result: AII amacrine cells in Dscaml1∆C/∆C mice show subtle disruption with normal cell density and no clustering, but increased Voronoi domain variance indicating irregular spacing.
evaluation: Claims C17-C21 demonstrate that DSCAML1-∆C disrupts PDZ binding (C17), retinas are modestly expanded (C18), AII cells have normal density (C19), no clustering (C20), but increased Voronoi variance (C21). Quantitative analyses (Figure 4H-K) support this subtle, intermediate phenotype.

result: VGLUT3-positive amacrine cells in Dscaml1∆C/∆C mice show severe phenotypes with increased cell density, disrupted spacing more severe than Bax-/- mutants, and aberrant neurite projections into the AII amacrine terminal region.
evaluation: Claims C22, C23, C26, C38-C40 show that VGLUT3 cells have increased density (C22), disrupted spacing (C23), more severe disruption than Bax-/- (C26), misprojected neurites (C38-C39), and significantly increased VGLUT3 area in the AII region (C40). Multiple quantitative measures (Figures 4O-R, 5I-L, 7O-R) provide strong support.

result: DSCAML1 promotes synapse maturation between rod bipolar cells and AII amacrine cells independent of C-terminal PDZ interactions, as dyad synapses appear normal in Dscaml1∆C/∆C but abnormal in Dscaml1-/- retinas.
evaluation: Claims C36, C37, C67, and C68 demonstrate that AII and RBC processes stratify normally (C36), dyad synapses are normal in ∆C mutants (C37), but abnormal in null mutants (C67), indicating PDZ-independent synapse maturation (C68). TEM analysis (Figure 7J-M) provides direct morphological evidence.

result: The requirement for PDZ-interacting C-termini of DSCAM and DSCAML1 varies by cell type, with some cell types showing complete dependence, others showing no dependence, and still others showing intermediate dependence, indicating multiple molecular mechanisms operate in different cellular contexts.
evaluation: Claims C41, C42, C70, C71, C81, C87, and C88 collectively establish the main conclusion that PDZ-dependence varies by cell type (C41-C42, C70-C71), DSCAMs function through multiple mechanisms (C81), and these must be defined cell-type specifically (C87-C88). The comprehensive phenotypic analysis across multiple cell types (Figures 2-7, Table 1) provides strong support for this differential dependence model.

result: Increased cell density from loss of developmental cell death contributes to but does not fully explain the spacing and fasciculation defects in ∆C mutants, as ipRGCs and VGLUT3 cells show more severe disruption than Bax-/- mutants despite comparable or lower cell densities.
evaluation: Claims C24-C26, C63-C64 demonstrate that ipRGCs are more clustered in ∆C than Bax-/- (C24), DA spacing is similar (C25), VGLUT3 spacing is more disrupted despite lower density (C26), and this pattern holds across cell types (C63-C64). Comparative analyses with Bax-/- mutants (Figures 5, 6) provide strong evidence that cell death is not the primary function.

result: DA cells and M1 ipRGCs co-fasciculate in Dscam∆C/∆C mutants, representing aberrant interactions between different cell types that normally co-stratify.
evaluation: Claims C34, C35, and C66 show that DA and M1 cells co-stratify correctly (C34), co-fasciculate in ∆C mutants (C35), and this is the only clear example of heterotypic co-fasciculation (C66). Imaging data (Figure 7C-E) and citation to prior work provide support for this observation.

result: Promotion of developmental cell death is not the sole primary function of Dscams, as self-avoidance defects persist even when cell density is controlled or reduced.
evaluation: Claims C62, C84, C85, and C86 establish that increased cell number can disrupt spacing (C62), but is not sufficient to explain self-avoidance defects (C84), cell death is not the sole function (C85), and clustering occurs even with reduced density (C86). Comparison with Bax-/- mutants and citation to prior work (Keeley et al., 2012; Fuerst et al., 2012) support this conclusion.

result: DSCAM shows little co-localization with multi-PDZ proteins in the adult IPL, but increased co-localization during development, indicating dynamic and transient interactions.
evaluation: Claims C82 and C83 report findings from de Andrade et al., 2014 showing developmental regulation of DSCAM-PDZ protein interactions. This is properly cited prior work that provides context for the current study's findings.

result: Background on Dscam/Dscaml1 structure, expression, function in self-avoidance and cell death, and known molecular interactions establishes the scientific context for the study.
evaluation: These claims (C1, C46-C59) provide established background information supported by appropriate citations to prior literature. They establish the known functions of Dscams and provide context for testing the role of PDZ interactions.

result: Drosophila Dscam1 and vertebrate Pcdhg achieve self-avoidance through extensive isoform diversity enabling self/non-self discrimination, a mechanism not available to vertebrate DSCAMs which lack such diversity.
evaluation: Claims C72-C80 describe well-established mechanisms in Drosophila Dscam1 (C72-C75) and Pcdhg (C76-C79) systems, properly cited to primary literature, and draw the logical inference that vertebrate DSCAMs cannot use this mechanism (C80). This provides important comparative context for understanding vertebrate DSCAM function.

result: The vertebrate retina provides an advantageous model system with ~100 neuronal cell types organized into layers and mosaic patterns.
evaluation: Claims C43-C45 provide standard background on retinal organization supported by established knowledge and appropriate citation (Masland, 2012). This establishes why the retina is a good model for studying neuronal organization.

result: Dscaml1 is expressed in rod circuit cells including rod photoreceptors, rod bipolar cells, and AII amacrine cells.
evaluation: Claim C16 reports established expression patterns from prior work (Fuerst et al., 2009), providing necessary background for interpreting the Dscaml1∆C/∆C phenotypes.

result: bNOS-positive amacrine cell organization in Dscam mutants varies with genetic background.
evaluation: Claim C65 reports prior findings (Fuerst et al., 2010) about genetic background effects, providing context for why bNOS cells were examined on a C57BL/6 background in the current study.

result: VGLUT3-positive amacrine cells normally stratify their neurites to the ON-OFF region of the IPL between ChAT-positive laminae.
evaluation: Claim C69 describes normal VGLUT3 cell stratification (Figure 7N), establishing the baseline for detecting misprojections in mutants. This is a straightforward descriptive observation.
